= Avro RPC
:artifactid: camel-avro-rpc-starter

Call and expose Apache Avro RPC services over HTTP or Netty.

== What's inside

* xref:{csb-camel-components}::avro-component.adoc[Avro RPC component], URI syntax: `avro:transport:host:port/messageName`

Please refer to the above links for usage and configuration details.

== Maven coordinates

[source,xml]
----
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.apache.camel.springboot</groupId>
    <artifactId>camel-avro-rpc-starter</artifactId>
</dependency>
----

== Spring Boot Auto-Configuration

The starter supports 12 options, which are listed below.

[width="100%",cols="2,5,^1,2",options="header"]
|===
| Name | Description | Default | Type
| camel.component.avro.autowired-enabled | Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc. | true | Boolean
| camel.component.avro.bridge-error-handler | Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored. | false | Boolean
| camel.component.avro.configuration | A shared configuration that every endpoint copies as its starting point. The options of the endpoint URI override its values. The option is a org.apache.camel.component.avro.AvroConfiguration type. |  | AvroConfiguration
| camel.component.avro.enabled | Whether to enable auto configuration of the avro component. This is enabled by default. |  | Boolean
| camel.component.avro.lazy-start-producer | Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing. | false | Boolean
| camel.component.avro.protocol | The Avro protocol (org.apache.avro.Protocol) that defines the messages, such as the PROTOCOL field of a class generated by the Avro compiler. Set this option or protocolClassName: the endpoint fails to start without a protocol. Camel adds the packages of the protocol to the trusted packages of Avro, which apply to the whole JVM: see serializablePackages. The option is a org.apache.avro.Protocol type. |  | Protocol
| camel.component.avro.protocol-class-name | The fully qualified name of the class that defines the protocol. For a class generated by the Avro compiler, its static PROTOCOL field is used; for any other class or interface, Avro reflection builds the protocol and reflectionProtocol is turned on. Ignored when protocol is set. Camel adds the package of the class to the trusted packages of Avro, which apply to the whole JVM: see serializablePackages. |  | String
| camel.component.avro.protocol-location | Not used: the component does not read this option. Use protocol or protocolClassName instead. |  | String
| camel.component.avro.reflection-protocol | Whether the protocol is a reflect protocol, built by Avro reflection from a Java interface, rather than one from classes generated by the Avro compiler. When true, the consumer and producer use the Avro reflect responder and requestor. Set it together with protocol: with protocolClassName it is turned on for a class without a PROTOCOL field. | false | Boolean
| camel.component.avro.serializable-packages | Comma-separated list of additional packages that contain trusted Avro model classes. Avro 1.12+ validates classes resolved from schemas; Camel automatically trusts org.apache.avro for IPC and packages derived from the configured protocol. Use this option for any additional model packages not inferred from the protocol. Avro has one class validator for the whole JVM. A package trusted by one endpoint is trusted for all Avro class resolution in the JVM, by every endpoint, Avro data format and Camel context, and stays trusted until the JVM is restarted: stopping the endpoint or the route does not remove it. |  | String
| camel.component.avro.single-parameter | Whether the consumer sets the message body to the one parameter of the called message, instead of an Object array of all parameters. The endpoint fails to start if the message, or any message of the protocol when messageName is not set, does not have exactly one parameter. | false | Boolean
| camel.component.avro.uri-authority | The authority (host and port) of the endpoint URI, which the component sets from the URI. Consumers with the same authority share one Avro server, created with the protocol of the first consumer that starts. A value set on the component is replaced by the authority of the endpoint URI. |  | String
|===
